cities.name: Shimla
cities.tagline: Queen of the Hills and Himachal Capital
cities.short_description: Shimla served as the summer capital of British India and features colonial architecture, pedestrian malls, and Himalayan vistas.
cities.description: Shimla is the capital city of Himachal Pradesh, situated along a ridge at an average elevation of 2,205 meters. It retains significant British colonial heritage including the Viceregal Lodge, Christ Church, and the UNESCO-inscribed Kalka-Shimla mountain railway.

places.name: The Ridge & Mall Road
places.summary: The open pedestrian esplanade forming the cultural and civic heart of Shimla.
places.short_description: Historic pedestrian promenade with Tudor-style architecture and sweeping views of the Pir Panjal ranges.
places.detailed_description: The Ridge is a large open public space running along the crest of Shimla, connecting to the famous Mall Road. It houses the neo-Gothic Christ Church, the state library, and water reservoirs serving the entire city.
places.visiting_hours: Open 24 hours (shops open 10:00 AM - 08:30 PM)
places.opening_hours: Open 24 hours
places.entry_fee: Free entry

places.name: Viceregal Lodge (Indian Institute of Advanced Study)
places.summary: Jacobethan-style former residence of the Viceroy of India, designed by Henry Irwin.
places.short_description: Historic 1888 estate on Observatory Hill where the Shimla Conference and Partition deliberations took place.
places.detailed_description: Constructed between 1880 and 1888 under Lord Dufferin, the Viceregal Lodge features solid grey limestone masonry, teak woodwork, and a historic indoor electric lighting system. Today it houses the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (IIAS).
places.address: Observatory Hill, Boileauganj, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171005
places.visiting_hours: 09:30 AM - 05:30 PM (Closed Mondays)
places.entry_fee: INR 50 (Indian), INR 200 (Foreign)
places.best_time_to_visit: March to June, September to November
places.source_name: Indian Institute of Advanced Study (Ministry of Education)

places.name: Christ Church Shimla
places.summary: The second oldest church in Northern India, designed in neo-Gothic style in 1857.
places.short_description: Iconic yellow neo-Gothic church on The Ridge featuring five historic stained-glass windows.
places.detailed_description: Consecrated in 1857, Christ Church was designed by J.T. Boileau in the neo-Gothic architectural style. Its five stained glass windows represent faith, hope, charity, fortitude, patience, and humility. It is an enduring architectural symbol of Shimla.
places.address: The Ridge, Mall Road, Shimla, Himachal Pradesh 171001
places.entry_fee: Free entry

cities.name: Manali
cities.tagline: High-Altitude Valley of Gods and Alpine Adventures
cities.short_description: High-altitude Himalayan township at the northern end of Kullu Valley, gateway to Lahaul and Ladakh.
cities.description: Manali is situated along the Beas River at 2,050 meters elevation in Kullu district. Known for deodar forests, ancient wooden pagodas, and adventure expeditions across Solang and the Atal Tunnel.

places.name: Hadimba Devi Temple (Dhungari Temple)
places.summary: Four-tiered wooden pagoda temple built in 1553 CE by Raja Bahadur Singh inside cedar forest.
places.short_description: Historic 16th-century wooden pagoda temple surrounded by cedar forest in Dhungari.
places.detailed_description: Built around a natural rock cave in 1553 CE, Hadimba Temple features intricate wood carvings of deities and animals, topped by a brass cone. It is dedicated to Hadimba, wife of Bhima from the Mahabharata.
places.address: Hadimba Temple Road, Dhungari, Manali, Himachal Pradesh 175131
places.entry_fee: Free entry
places.best_time_to_visit: March to June, September to December

places.name: Solang Valley
places.summary: Side valley at the top of Kullu Valley known for summer paragliding and winter skiing.
places.short_description: Famed alpine valley offering adventure sports, cable car rides, and snow fields.
places.detailed_description: Situated 14 km northwest of Manali at an elevation of 2,560 m, Solang Valley is Himachal principal hub for winter snow sports, ski instruction, paragliding, and cable-car journeys against snow-capped peaks.
places.entry_fee: Free entry to valley (Activity fees separate)
places.best_time_to_visit: December to March (snow), April to June (paragliding)

cities.name: Spiti Valley
cities.tagline: The Middle Land of Ancient Gompas and Cold Desert Landscapes
cities.short_description: Cold desert mountain valley situated high in the Himalayas, housing millennium-old Buddhist monasteries.
cities.description: Spiti Valley is an expansive high-altitude cold desert valley located at an average altitude of 3,800 meters in Lahaul and Spiti district. It is famous for thousand-year-old Tibetan Buddhist monasteries including Tabo and Key, fossil villages, and Chandratal wetland.

places.name: Key Monastery (Kye Gompa)
places.summary: Iconic 11th-century Tibetan Buddhist monastery perched on a conical hill at 4,166 m.
places.short_description: Spectacular fortress-like monastery of the Gelugpa sect perched above the Spiti River.
places.detailed_description: Founded in the 11th century by Dromt├╢n, Key Monastery is the largest monastery in Spiti Valley. Built in the Pasada style with fortress-like tiered rooms, it houses ancient thangkas, manuscripts, and murals, serving over 300 resident lamas.
places.entry_fee: Free entry (Donations accepted)

sources.evidence_note: Official tourism portal Spiti circuit guide.

places.name: Tabo Monastery (Ajanta of the Himalayas)
places.place_type: Ancient Mud-Brick Gompa & UNESCO Tentative Site
places.summary: Founded in 996 CE by Rinchen Zangpo, famous for preserved 10th-century stucco sculptures and frescoes.
places.short_description: Millennium-old mud-brick monastic complex on the UNESCO Tentative List, renowned as the Ajanta of the Himalayas.
places.detailed_description: Founded in the Tibetan Year of the Fire Ape (996 CE) by translator Rinchen Zangpo under the king of Guge, Tabo is the oldest continuously operating Buddhist enclave in India. Its nine temples preserve wall paintings and clay sculptures of the Vajradhatu mandala.
places.entry_fee: Free entry
places.contact_information: Archaeological Survey of India Shimla Circle: 0177-2652251
places.heritage_status: UNESCO Tentative List & ASI Monument of National Importance

sources.evidence_note: Official UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List inscription.

places.name: Chandratal Lake (Moon Lake)
places.summary: Crescent-shaped high-altitude alpine lake located at 4,250 m on the Samudra Tapu plateau.
places.short_description: Pristine crescent-shaped glacial lake and designated Ramsar wetland in Spiti Valley.
places.detailed_description: Situated at 4,250 meters elevation, Chandratal is a designated Ramsar wetland of international importance. The lake changes color from turquoise to deep emerald through the day and is framed by the Chandra Bhaga mountain range.
places.address: Samudra Tapu Plateau, Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175140
places.visiting_hours: Sunrise to Sunset (Daylight hours only)
places.entry_fee: Free entry (Eco-tourism fee collected at Batal checkpost)

heritage.summary: Founded in 996 CE by Rinchen Zangpo, famous for preserved 10th-century stucco sculptures and frescoes.
heritage.short_description: Millennium-old mud-brick monastic complex on the UNESCO Tentative List, renowned as the Ajanta of the Himalayas.
heritage.detailed_description: Founded in the Tibetan Year of the Fire Ape (996 CE) by translator Rinchen Zangpo under the king of Guge, Tabo is the oldest continuously operating Buddhist enclave in India. Its nine temples preserve wall paintings and clay sculptures of the Vajradhatu mandala.
heritage.entry_fee: Free entry
heritage.contact_information: Archaeological Survey of India Shimla Circle: 0177-2652251
heritage.heritage_status: UNESCO Tentative List & ASI Monument of National Importance

sources.evidence_note: Official UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List inscription.

religious_cultural.name: Key Monastery (Kye Gompa)
religious_cultural.summary: Iconic 11th-century Tibetan Buddhist monastery perched on a conical hill at 4,166 m.
religious_cultural.short_description: Spectacular fortress-like monastery of the Gelugpa sect perched above the Spiti River.
religious_cultural.detailed_description: Founded in the 11th century by Dromt├╢n, Key Monastery is the largest monastery in Spiti Valley. Built in the Pasada style with fortress-like tiered rooms, it houses ancient thangkas, manuscripts, and murals, serving over 300 resident lamas.

sources.evidence_note: Official tourism portal Spiti circuit guide.

nature_parks_zoo.name: Chandratal Lake (Moon Lake)
nature_parks_zoo.summary: Crescent-shaped high-altitude alpine lake located at 4,250 m on the Samudra Tapu plateau.
nature_parks_zoo.short_description: Pristine crescent-shaped glacial lake and designated Ramsar wetland in Spiti Valley.
nature_parks_zoo.detailed_description: Situated at 4,250 meters elevation, Chandratal is a designated Ramsar wetland of international importance. The lake changes color from turquoise to deep emerald through the day and is framed by the Chandra Bhaga mountain range.
nature_parks_zoo.address: Samudra Tapu Plateau, Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175140

cities.tagline: Seat of the Dalai Lama and Gateway to Dhauladhar
cities.short_description: Scenic hillside city in Kangra district, home to the Central Tibetan Administration and HPCA Stadium.
cities.description: Dharamshala is situated on the lower slopes of the Dhauladhar range. It is divided into lower Dharamshala and upper McLeod Ganj, serving as the residence of the 14th Dalai Lama and headquarters of Tibetan culture in exile.

cities.name: Kangra
cities.tagline: Ancient Capital of Nagarkot and Majestic Himalayan Forts
cities.short_description: Historic town on the Baner and Majhi rivers, home to the Kangra Fort and Bajreshwari Temple.
cities.description: Kangra was the capital of the Katoch dynasty, one of the oldest surviving royal dynasties in the world. The town is famous for Kangra Fort, the Bajreshwari Devi Shaktipeeth, and close proximity to the 8th-century Masrur Rock Cut Temples.

places.name: Kangra Fort (Nagarkot)
places.summary: The largest fort in the Himalayas and one of the oldest dated forts in India, founded by the Katoch dynasty.
places.short_description: Massive ancient citadel perched at the confluence of the Banganga and Majhi rivers.
places.detailed_description: Built by the Katoch royal dynasty, Kangra Fort spans over 4 kilometers of fortifications. It withstood sieges by Mahmud of Ghazni, Jahangir, and Maharaja Ranjit Singh before being damaged in the 1905 earthquake. It preserves stone gateways, courtyards, and the Ambika Devi temple.
places.entry_fee: INR 25 (Indian), INR 300 (Foreign)
places.contact_information: Archaeological Survey of India Shimla Circle: 0177-2652251
places.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India / District Administration Kangra
places.audit_note: Verified live HTTP 200 on 2026-09-10. Title: "Kangra Fort | District Kangra, Government of Himachal Pradesh | India"

places.name: Masrur Rock Cut Temples (Himalayan Pyramid)
places.place_type: Monolithic Rock Cut Temple Complex & UNESCO Tentative Site
places.summary: 8th-century early medieval complex of 15 monolithic rock-cut temples carved out of a single sandstone ridge.
places.short_description: Rare 8th-century monolithic rock-cut temple complex carved out of living sandstone with reflection pond.
places.detailed_description: Dating to the 8th century CE, the Masrur temples are an extraordinary example of North Indian Nagara style monolithic architecture carved directly from a natural sandstone hill. Positioned facing the snow peaks of the Dhauladhar, the complex includes a rectangular sacred water tank.
places.address: Masrur, Lahalpur, Kangra District, Himachal Pradesh 176049
places.entry_fee: INR 25 (Indian), INR 300 (Foreign)
places.heritage_status: UNESCO Tentative List & ASI Monument of National Importance

places.name: Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP)
places.place_type: UNESCO World Heritage National Park & Biosphere Reserve
places.summary: UNESCO World Heritage site protecting high alpine peaks, alpine meadows, and endangered fauna.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage national park protecting Western Himalayan biodiversity and endangered species like the Western Tragopan.
places.detailed_description: Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014, GHNP spans 1,171 sq km across elevations from 1,500 to 6,000 m. It protects pristine alpine meadows, glacial valleys, and over 800 plant species, serving as a vital sanctuary for the snow leopard and blue sheep.

cities.name: Jaipur
cities.city_type: State Capital & UNESCO World Heritage City
cities.tagline: The Pink City of Forts, Observatories and Royal Palaces
cities.short_description: Capital of Rajasthan, famous for pink terracotta facades, Amber Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar.
cities.description: Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, Jaipur was designed on Vastu Shastra principles by Vidyadhar Bhattacharya. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage City in 2019, it features Amber Fort, City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar.

places.name: Amber Palace (Amer Fort)
places.summary: 16th-century red sandstone and marble fort palace built by Raja Man Singh I, inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage list.
places.short_description: Majestic UNESCO World Heritage hill fort overlooking Maota Lake, famous for the Sheesh Mahal mirror palace.
places.detailed_description: Situated on Cheel ka Teela above Maota Lake, Amber Fort is constructed from pale yellow and pink sandstone with white marble. Its Sheesh Mahal (Hall of Mirrors) reflects light across concave glass mosaics. Inscribed as part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan UNESCO site in 2013.
places.visiting_hours: 08:00 AM - 05:30 PM, Evening Light & Sound: 06:30 PM - 09:00 PM
places.entry_fee: INR 100 (Indian), INR 500 (Foreign)
places.heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Hill Forts of Rajasthan, 2013)

sources.evidence_note: Official UNESCO World Heritage List serial inscription 247 for Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

sources.source_name: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Rajasthan

places.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
places.summary: Five-story pink sandstone palace built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh with 953 jharokhas.
places.short_description: Honeycomb-like five-story facade featuring 953 intricately carved casements built to allow royal women to view street festivals.
places.detailed_description: Designed by Lal Chand Ustad in the form of the crown of Krishna, Hawa Mahal is constructed of red and pink sandstone. Its 953 jharokhas (casements) create a Venturi breeze effect that keeps the chambers cool even during peak summer.
places.address: Hawa Mahal Road, Badi Choupad, J.D.A. Market, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302002
places.entry_fee: INR 50 (Indian), INR 200 (Foreign)
places.heritage_status: State Protected Monument & Landmark of Jaipur UNESCO Walled City
places.attribution: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Rajasthan

sources.evidence_note: Official state tourism profile for Hawa Mahal.

sources.source_name: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Rajasthan

places.name: Jantar Mantar Observatory
places.summary: 18th-century stone astronomical observatory built by Sawai Jai Singh II, housing the world largest stone sundial.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage site housing 19 architectural astronomical instruments including the giant Samrat Yantra sundial.
places.detailed_description: Completed in 1734 by Rajput king Sawai Jai Singh II, Jantar Mantar features 19 architectural astronomical instruments made of local stone and marble. The Vrihat Samrat Yantra is the world largest stone sundial, measuring time to an accuracy of two seconds.
places.address: Gangori Bazaar, J.D.A. Market, Pink City, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302002
places.entry_fee: INR 50 (Indian), INR 200 (Foreign)
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (mid-day recommended for shadow instruments)
places.contact_information: Archaeological Survey of India Jaipur Circle: 0141-2704257

sources.evidence_note: Official UNESCO World Heritage list entry 1338 for Jantar Mantar Jaipur.

cities.name: Udaipur
cities.tagline: City of Lakes, Palaces and Mewar Valour
cities.short_description: Historic capital of the Mewar kingdom, famous for Lake Pichola, City Palace, and island palaces.
cities.description: Founded in 1559 by Maharana Udai Singh II, Udaipur is situated around Lake Pichola, Fateh Sagar, and Swaroop Sagar. It features the massive City Palace complex, Jag Mandir, and Saheliyon-ki-Bari.

places.name: City Palace Complex Udaipur
places.summary: The largest royal palace complex in Rajasthan, built over 400 years on the banks of Lake Pichola.
places.short_description: Colossal marble and granite palace complex with panoramic vistas over Lake Pichola, housing the Mewar Museum.
places.detailed_description: Constructed beginning in 1559 by Maharana Udai Singh II, the City Palace blends Rajasthani and Mughal architectural styles. Standing on the east bank of Lake Pichola, it encompasses eleven palaces, courtyards, hanging gardens, and the famous Mor Chowk (Peacock Courtyard).
places.entry_fee: INR 300 (Adult), INR 100 (Child)

cities.name: Tawang
cities.tagline: Land of Monasteries and Sela Pass
cities.short_description: High-altitude mountain town at 3,048 meters elevation, home to the historic 17th-century Tawang Monastery.
cities.description: Tawang is situated in the northwestern corner of Arunachal Pradesh at an elevation of 3,048 meters. It is famous for Tawang Monastery (the largest in India and second largest in the world), Sela Pass, and picturesque high-altitude alpine lakes.

places.name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgey Lhatse)
places.summary: The largest monastery in India and second largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso.
places.short_description: Fortress-like Mahayana Buddhist monastery perched at 3,000 meters elevation, housing an 18-foot gilded Buddha statue.
places.detailed_description: Founded in 1680-81 CE by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso in accordance with the wishes of the 5th Dalai Lama, Tawang Monastery belongs to the Gelug school. The monastery resembles a fortified castle commanding views of the Tawang-Chu valley. It houses an 18-foot gilded statue of Buddha, a three-story library of sacred Kangyur scriptures, and valuable thangkas.
places.visiting_hours: 07:00 AM - 05:00 PM (Morning prayers: 07:00 AM)
places.entry_fee: Free entry (Museum fee INR 20)
places.best_time_to_visit: March to October (Torgya festival in January)

places.name: Sela Pass & Sela Lake
places.summary: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m elevation, connecting Tawang to the rest of India.
places.short_description: Majestic mountain pass at 13,700 feet with prayer flags, snow-capped peaks, and the sacred Sela Lake.
places.detailed_description: Sela Pass is situated at an elevation of 4,170 meters (13,700 ft) on the border between Tawang and West Kameng districts. It features the sacred Paradise Lake (Sela Lake) which freezes in winter, framed by hundreds of Buddhist prayer flags fluttering against Himalayan peaks.
places.visiting_hours: Daylight hours only (Sunrise to Sunset)
places.entry_fee: Free entry (Inner Line Permit required for Arunachal Pradesh)
